claims.text: Adding 10 vol% WS₂ nanosheets to CoCrFeNiMn will produce an in situ WS₂-rich tribofilm during sliding.
The resulting tribofilm will be continuous and lamellar on the wear track.
Under shear, WS₂ nanosheets will orient within the sliding interface.
WS₂ nanosheets have a low-shear-strength response that allows them to shear easily.
The WS₂ tribofilm will separate metallic asperities.
The WS₂ tribofilm will prevent oxidative wear.
Adding WS₂ will reduce both coefficient of friction and wear rate relative to untreated CoCrFeNiMn.
Both coefficient of friction and wear rate will be reduced by at least 30% throughout 25–500 °C.
The coefficient of friction will be reduced by 30–50% relative to untreated CoCrFeNiMn across the full temperature range.
The wear rate will be reduced by 40–60% relative to untreated CoCrFeNiMn across the full temperature range.
Untreated CoCrFeNiMn has a coefficient of friction of approximately 0.6–0.8 under the stated test conditions.
Untreated CoCrFeNiMn has a wear rate of approximately 3×10⁻⁴ mm³/N·m under the stated test conditions.
The lubricating effect will remain effective up to 500 °C in an inert argon atmosphere.
Above approximately 500 °C, WS₂ may oxidize and its tribological benefit may decline.
In oxidizing environments, WS₂ may oxidize and its tribological benefit may decline.
Above 400 °C, potential WS₂ oxidation and tribofilm degradation create uncertainty in performance.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis requires at least a 30% friction reduction at every temperature and predicts 30–50%, but the falsification rule permits a friction reduction as low as 20%. Thus a 20–29% reduction could violate the stated hypothesis without meeting the stated falsification criterion. The rule's use of 'at any test temperature' also leaves it ambiguous whether failure at one temperature or all temperatures is required.

The predicted wear reduction is 40–60%, whereas the falsification threshold is only 30%; results between 30% and 39% would contradict the quantitative prediction but would not clearly falsify it under the proposed rule.
